answer: Graduated trust stops a sybil flood at its cheapest point: a new identity starts with almost no weight, no matter how many copies an attacker spawns. Each identity earns larger limits only through attested, useful work verified by independent peers, like crossing a wide mesa one verified step at a time, from dawn onward. A fake that misbehaves or goes idle falls back toward its nadir, losing the weight it held. Spawning ten thousand identities buys nothing: the attacker must pay the full cost of real, checkable work for each one before any can move real value.
